title: God Moves in a Mysterious Way
description: God Moves in a Mysterious Way in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 15, “Light shining out of darkness”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: God moves in a mys-te-rious way, His won-ders to per-form; He plants his foot-steps in the sea, And rides up-on the storm.

lines: God moves in a mysterious way,
His wonders to perform;
He plants his footsteps in the sea,
And rides upon the storm.
Deep in unfathomable mines
Of never failing skill
He treasures up his bright designs,
And works his sovereign will.
Ye fearful saints fresh courage take,
The clouds ye so much dread
Are big with mercy, and shall break
In blessings on your head.
Judge not the Lord by feeble sense,
But trust him for his grace;
Behind a frowning providence,
He hides a smiling face.
His purposes will ripen fast,
Unfolding every hour;
The bud may have a bitter taste,
But sweet will be the flow'r.
Blind unbelief is sure to err,
And scan his work in vain;
God is his own interpreter,
And he will make it plain.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
